item.text: {"winner":"B","confidence":"high","summary":"B is preferable because it solves retry-safe Upload with focused buffering and stronger contract-oriented tests, while A makes broad, unnecessary changes to raw request replay and reader ownership. Both patches violate the frozen contract by adding association APIs and bypassing FilesService.Add.","reasons":["B tests multipart field/name/content, retrying content streamed from an *os.File, pre-request validation, and source-reader error propagation; A lacks the required source-reader-error test and its Upload retry test uses strings.Reader rather than streamed content.","B confines replayability to the SDK-built multipart body, consistent with the established bytes.Reader pattern. A alters RawClient.Do globally, including seekable-body ownership, Content-Length calculation, and retry behavior, despite the contract explicitly prohibiting retry-machinery refactoring.","A's seekable replay implementation reuses and seeks the same underlying reader for every GetBody call, introducing shared-position and concurrency risks beyond this feature.","B explicitly verifies identical complete multipart bodies across retry attempts and verifies existing request options are preserved."],"risks_a":["Upload calls Raw.Do directly instead of routing through FilesService.Add, duplicating request construction, decoding, and error handling.","Adds prohibited association form fields and a new WithFilesFormFields API, using NewFileWithFields instead of the required NewFile helper.","Changes global Raw.Do semantics and stops transports from closing seekable bodies, creating compatibility and resource-lifecycle risk outside file uploads."],"risks_b":["Upload also calls Raw.Do directly rather than FilesService.Add, violating the central frozen design requirement.","Adds six prohibited public association options and extends multipart machinery unnecessarily; their comments incorrectly say they apply to Add even though Add ignores cfg.form.","Uses NewFileWithFields rather than directly reusing multipartbody.NewFile as required."]}
